deployment.mechanism: manual MSI installer (official nodejs.org Windows x64 .msi, run by hand — not nvm-windows, not winget-installed)
deployment.mechanism_evidence: Verified 2026-09-08, read-only, live host: (1) no nvm — no `nvm` command, no NVM_HOME/NVM_SYMLINK env vars, no nvm install directories; (2) `C:\Program Files\nodejs` is a real directory, not a symlink/junction (nvm-windows would symlink this path); (3) registry Uninstall entry has WindowsInstaller=1, ProductCode {6178C0C7-8EA8-458F-8060-E49E500A666F}, InstallSource 'C:\Users\Matt Becker\Downloads\'; (4) the exact installer file (node-v24.18.0-x64.msi, retained in Downloads, dated 2026-07-07) carries that same ProductCode in its own Property table, read via the WindowsInstaller COM API in read-only mode. `winget list --id OpenJS.NodeJS` does match this install for upgrade-tracking, but that reflects winget's ARP-matching against its package database, not the install method — InstallSource is Matt's own Downloads folder, not winget's cache.
deployment.update_behavior: In-place replace, not a side-install. The installed MSI has a populated UpgradeCode — the Windows Installer field that drives the standard major-upgrade sequence (RemoveExistingProducts against any prior ProductCode sharing that UpgradeCode) when a newer MSI is run. Confirmed read-only against the retained 24.18.0 installer's own Property table via the WindowsInstaller COM `OpenDatabase` API (opens the file, installs nothing), then re-confirmed 2026-09-08 against the downloaded v24.20.0 target MSI before Matt applied it — both carry UpgradeCode {47C07A3A-42EF-4213-A85D-8F5A59077C28}. The real update ran 2026-09-08 (run `20260908-220239`): registry confirms the live install now carries ProductCode {DC5BBE4F-0668-40DC-A913-83710DA79E35}, DisplayVersion 24.20.0, InstallSource still Matt's own Downloads folder — in-place replace behaved exactly as predicted.
